Header:
Date: 2026-06-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Ramirez (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Redwood Prod), Priya Singh (AuroraCloud PM), Ethan Moore (Cloud Engineer), Sofia De la Cruz (Solutions Arch), Raj Patel (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood and AuroraCloud walked through technical requirements for a marketplace listing and joint reference architecture. Key topics: packaging (AMI vs container), terraform and onboarding automation, VPC/private deployment networking, billing/metering integration, SSO and compliance artifacts, benchmark plan for performance/latency validation. Action items and next steps captured below.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, i'm maya from redwood, i'll run the agenda, Luca is our se, Anika is on product.
[00:18] Priya: thanks maya, morning afternoon, it's priya, i'm the partner pm, we've got ethan and sofia on the call to cover engineering and arch.
[00:29] Luca: quick note, we want to be pragmatic - marketplace listing is two parts: the SKU + listing metadata, and a validated deployment artifact (ami/container + terraform) so customers can onboard fast.
[00:45] Ethan: sounds good, question right away - for auroracloud landing zones, should we expect a vpc peering flow or private link? currently we do vpn tunnels but want to support vpc peering for lower latency.
[01:02] Maya: good q; both supported. for hosted marketplace integration we typically recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink if you need cross-account private connectivity. for the redwood private deployment package we have an on-prem AMI and also a containerized helm chart; luca, should we talk images?
[01:22] Luca: yeah, so two validated delivery options: OCI container + Helm for k8s, and an AMI for customers who want dedicated instances. the reference-arch doc will show both patterns; note that the AMI includes prebuilt runtime and quantized models for typical configs, but customers can swap model versions.
[01:40] Sofia: on quantization - how do you handle q4/q8 variants and model fallbacks? some of our customers will need lower latency with slightly lower quality.
[01:53] Luca: we expose model variants in the listing via metadata and we support routing policy in runtime. so you can list default model = redwood-rlhf-1, and alternative variants q4/opt. runtime handles fallback and routing rules (latency vs cost). small aside the transcript might call it R-L-H-F sometimes we see r-l-f-h, sorry.
[02:15] Raj: security check - we need SOC2 report, key management details (kms/hms?), and audit logs retention policy. also SSO/SSO metadata for SAML.
[02:30] Maya: yes, we'll attach SOC2 and ISO artifacts. we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments and support both AWS KMS and external HSM via KMIP for on-prem. audit logs are available via console and can be exported to cloud storage or SIEM. SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported.
[02:48] Priya: good. on marketplace commercials - we need SKU model for metering; do you emit per-token billing events or HTTP request based?
[03:02] Luca: we emit usage events per invocation with token counts; for marketplace we can also provide a metering shim so the marketplace can ingest usage records. we'll provide sample webhook and csv export.
[03:17] Ethan: terraform - can you share a sample repo? we prefer to validate via our CI and run automated smoke tests.
[03:27] Maya: yes we'll share the terraform module and a smoke test harness. Luca, link?
[03:33] Luca: i'll upload the reference repo to the partner bucket; it includes an example terraform module, helm values, and smoke test script that exercises model inference at 512 tokens. link: https://redwood.example.com/partner-artifacts/auroracloud/terraform.zip (note: placeholder).
[03:51] Sofia: network egress - can redwood runtime operate entirely inside our vpc or does it need egress for licensing/telemetry?
[04:05] Luca: for private deployments no external egress required if you opt-in for fully air-gapped mode. for hosted/dedicated we do periodic telemetry pings but those can be disabled. licensing checks can be done via offline tokens.
[04:20] Priya: regulatory notes - we have EU customers with data residency needs; do you support region pinning and per-tenant data isolation?
[04:32] Maya: yes, region pinning and dedicated capacity available (Redwood Dedicated). for marketplace reference arch we'll show GCP/AWS region options and how to pin.
[04:45] Raj: can we get a list of all compliance artifacts up front? also encryption at rest details for embeddings and KV cache.
[04:57] Luca: sure - encryption at rest is AES-256; KV cache is encrypted in transit and at rest; we can swap to customer-managed keys via KMS. i'll add the full list to the package.
[05:10] Priya: great. next, UI/console - for marketplace listing will you provide screenshots and per-route dashboards?
[05:21] Anika: yes, we can provide console screenshots, per-route cost/latency dashboards, and a short video walkthrough for the listing. we'll also include a sample secrets store integration doc.
[05:34] Ethan: benchmarks - we want to run a joint benchmark for latency at 1k rps and evaluate cost per token. is that realistic?
[05:44] Luca: for an initial benchmark, let's do a staged plan: smoke tests (single instance), scale tests (multi-node), and long-run stability. 1k rps might need dedicated capacity; we'll help size it. we'll run at 512 and 1024 token profiles.
[06:00] Priya: timeline - auroracloud want listing live in marketplace by july 15 if possible. are these dates realistic?
[06:09] Maya: tight but doable. main blocking items: security reviews and terraform validation. if we get artifacts this week we can target a staging listing by 7/1 and GA by 7/15.
[06:22] Raj: also legal - need to loop in our procurement team for revenue share and terms.
[06:30] Priya: yep, i'll add them.
[06:35] Luca: operational notes - our reference-arch will include observability hooks: prometheus metrics, trace ids, and export to your SIEM. recommended retention settings and cost controls included.
[06:50] Sofia: question re: model updates - how do we handle breaking changes in model outputs? we need a regression test suite.
[07:00] Anika: we support eval hooks and prompt sets; you'll be able to pin model versions and we provide quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval prompts. we'll share the eval harness.
[07:15] Maya: ok wrapping to logistics - action items listed. quick recap of artifacts we'll share: listing checklist, terraform + helm repo, reference-arch diagram, compliance pack, benchmark plan, console screenshots, eval harness.
[07:33] Priya: sounds good, thanks. one last thing - could you include a short blurb we can reuse on our marketplace listing re: support and SLA?
[07:42] Maya: yes we have a standard "Redwood Supported by Redwood Inference" blurb and SLA matrix. we'll include.
[07:50] Ethan: can we schedule the engineering benchmark for week of 6/22, maybe tuesday?
[07:57] Maya: tentatively tuesday 6/23 16:00 UTC, i'll send calendar invite after this call.
[08:05] Priya: great, thanks all.
